claim: The server's Web.config AppSetting VideoProcessingPath (read into AzureFFMpegV2._processingPath) must equal the Python video worker's processing.work_dir (D:\Media\motion\v2 on abydos) because server and worker exchange files through that shared directory; misalignment yields VP Status=InvokeFailed with 'No such file or directory' on the ffmpeg -i input.
trigger: when VideoProduction rows show Status=InvokeFailed and the LogFile reports 'No such file or directory' on the -i input
before changing VideoProcessingPath in Web.config or processing.work_dir in video-worker config.json

claim: A server-team session recorded three nimbus learnings: learning_94d (AzureFile.getStream invariant), learning_574 (VideoProcessingPath alignment), and learning_9ca (cleanup_on_complete post-mortem trap).
trigger: when searching project nimbus for server-team learnings about AzureFile.getStream, VideoProcessingPath, or cleanup_on_complete

claim: On OVH bridge .47 the server returned token:null from /api/Frame/requestArtAccess for every call even though correctly-oriented crop-{frameId}-*.mp4 files existed on disk, so bridges fell back to getRawContent and displayed source JPGs in the wrong orientation — the VP pipeline never delivered crops to any consumer since deployment.
trigger: when a Meural displays wrong-orientation content despite correct Frames.Rotate values and correct crop MP4s on disk
when bridge logs show requestArtAccess responses with token:null and repeated getRawContent fallbacks

claim: Declaring a pipeline 'green end-to-end' requires verification at the final consumer boundary (e.g. a bridge actually displaying produced content), not just that a producer stage wrote an output file — job 573139's crop-584-1.mp4 on disk proved only gate 1 of 3 while requestArtAccess still returned token:null.
trigger: before declaring a multi-stage pipeline green based on a single stage's completion report
when a VP job completion shows an output file exists but no consumer-side delivery check was run

claim: requestArtAccess returned token=null because ArtVideo.getCachedFilePath computes the cache path as crop-{frameId}-{ld?.version ?? 0}.mp4 and the layout version at read time differed from the version in effect when the worker produced the file, so the exact-path AzureFile.exists check failed; the same ld?.version pattern exists in ImageFile.cs:697 and VideoFile.cs:1220.
trigger: when requestArtAccess returns token:null while a crop-{frameId}-{ver}.mp4 exists on disk
when ArtVideoCache.LayoutVersion disagrees with the version suffix embedded in its BlobPath

claim: picFrame.ArtVideoCache is keyed per-frame by unique constraint (MediaId, ProfileId, Target=frame.Id) and reads prefer ArtVideoCache.BlobPath via Media.tryGetCachedBlob, falling back to the constructed crop-{frameId}-{ld.version}.mp4 path; the migration AddArtVideoCacheTarget.sql is applied on stargate MySQL but must still run on Azure SQL before any future Azure prod deploy.
trigger: before any future Azure prod deploy of picFrameWeb (run AddArtVideoCacheTarget.sql first)
when debugging requestArtAccess crop lookups through ArtVideoCache

claim: All 3,331 pre-migration ArtVideoCache rows have Target=0 and will never match per-frame (MediaId, ProfileId, Target=frame.Id) lookups, so after the Target deploy each (media,frame) pair's first request misses the cache and triggers a fresh VP job — a one-time warm-up burst, not a problem.
trigger: when a burst of new VideoProduction jobs appears after the ArtVideoCache Target column deploy
when per-frame ArtVideoCache lookups miss for media that previously had ready cache rows

claim: After the 2026-04-14 server deploy, the MQTT config delivered to freshly-connecting frames was a 127-byte payload without KeyValues.accessKey, so any OVH frame that reconnected had no accessKey and got HTTP 401 on every requestArtAccess call while frames still holding a pre-deploy in-memory accessKey kept working.
trigger: when bridge picFrame.log shows 'Applying MQTT config (KeyValues present: false)' and MediaGetter repeats 'got null data for media definition'
when curl from a bridge returns HTTP 401 on /api/Frame/requestArtAccess after a reboot or reconnect

claim: The retained MQTT topic frame/{uuid}/config had two incompatible writers — Frame.PublishConfigRetainedAsync (rich payload with KeyValues including accessKey) and DeviceConfigPublisher.PublishFrameConfig (flat ~127-byte payload with no KeyValues) — so any PublishBridgeConfig run clobbered the retained config and frames reconnecting afterward 401'd on requestArtAccess.
trigger: when a reconnecting frame receives a ~127-byte frame/{uuid}/config retained payload with no KeyValues
when frames begin returning HTTP 401 on requestArtAccess after a bridge claim, rename, pair, or admin bridge-config push

claim: WebUser.getAdminId() at picFrameWeb/WebUser.cs:40 casts Session["user"] and dereferences it without a null check, throwing NullReferenceException before the WebAdminUser fallback runs, which breaks admin WebMethods for sessions that only populate SessionVariables.WebAdminUser.
trigger: when an admin [WebMethod] using WebUser.CheckAdmin returns an error despite an authenticated admin browser session
before writing a new admin WebMethod that relies on WebUser.getAdminId or CheckAdmin

claim: After the 2026-04-14 DeviceConfigPublisher KeyValues fix restored auth, every requestArtAccess response returned full-0-0.jpg token URLs (zero crop-*.mp4 hits in full-day bridge logs, even for mediaType=video), leaving it unverified whether the ArtVideoCache per-frame Target fix actually delivers MP4 crops.
trigger: when verifying the ArtVideoCache.BlobPath fix by grepping bridge logs for 'crop-' or '.mp4'
when requestArtAccess returns full-0-0.jpg URLs for mediaType=video requests

claim: NimbusVideoWorker pushes results as LPUSH video:result:{jobId} with a 1-hour EXPIRE and no durable DB writeback, so if the enqueuing C# caller dies before its BRPOP, the result key expires unread and the ArtVideoCache row stays Status=processing even though the worker completed and the output MP4 sits in D:\Media\motion\v2.
trigger: when ArtVideoCache rows stay Status=processing while the worker log shows 'Pushed result to Redis' and 'completed successfully'
when KEYS video:result:* returns nothing for jobs the worker reported completing

claim: A coordinator who parks immediately after delegating a time-sensitive test can miss an urgent blocker reply for 20+ minutes, so stay in-session until the delegated team reports back, and fetch a specifically-named pending message by message_id rather than relying on a limit-capped message list.
trigger: before parking right after delegating a time-sensitive test to another team
when a state spec's Next Steps names a specific pending message to read on resume

claim: As of 2026-04-15 ConfigGroups (10 rows, byte-for-byte with Azure) and MqttRouting (8 rows, intentionally diverged to ActiveServer='abydos-staging') are already seeded on stargate MySQL, and MqttRouting must never be re-seeded from Azure because that would route all MQTT traffic back to Azure and break frame comms.
trigger: before seeding or re-syncing ConfigGroups or MqttRouting tables on stargate MySQL
when executing cutover-steps.sh Step 3.5 or any NimbusSync run that could touch MqttRouting

claim: Stargate MySQL's picFrame schema had none of Azure SQL's triggers; only trg_Frames_AutoGenerateCredentials (which sets MqttUsername/MqttPassword/AccessKey on Frames INSERT, ported as BEFORE INSERT with UPPER(UUID())) was ported on 2026-04-15, it is not in source control, and a NimbusSync table recreate would silently drop it and make new OVH pairs fail again.
trigger: when a newly-paired OVH frame has NULL MqttUsername/MqttPassword/AccessKey
after NimbusSync-full drops or recreates picFrame tables on stargate
when an auto-populated column is NULL on OVH rows but set on Azure-originated rows

claim: getAzureSASToken on the post-2026-04-14 server unconditionally returns the literal 4-character body "null", which survives a Trim('"') check, so mobile's GetAzureSasTokenAsync must detect body=="null" and return null so MediaUploadService falls back to api/mobile/uploadMedia instead of attempting an Azure Blob upload with an empty SAS (Azure 401 NoAuthenticationInformation).
trigger: when mobile uploads fail with Azure 401 NoAuthenticationInformation
before parsing the getAzureSASToken response body in mobile upload code

claim: getMediaList (MobileController.cs:1190) indicates video via the mediaType integer field (0=jpg, 1=gif, 2=video) while contentType only identifies the container (Account/Art/Playlist), so mobile must parse mediaType (PlaylistMediaItem.IsVideo == mediaType 2) to flag video thumbnails.
trigger: when video items from getMediaList are not flagged as video in the mobile app
before parsing ContentDescription JSON fields in GetPlaylistMediaAsync or GetMyArtAsync

claim: A CollectionView with ItemSizingStrategy="MeasureFirstItem" caches the first item's measured size so bound HeightRequest changes in the DataTemplate never re-layout subsequent items; MeasureAllItems is required (at a perf cost) for the PhotosPage thumb-size slider to work.
trigger: when bound HeightRequest changes in a CollectionView DataTemplate do not visually resize items
before adding a size-binding control such as a thumb-size slider to a CollectionView page

claim: nimbus-agent handlePairMeural (internal/meural/commands.go:147-211) unconditionally returns success=false ALREADY_PAIRED for already-paired Meurals with no credential-refresh fall-through, so the server cannot push refreshed MQTT credentials to an existing Meural; the workaround is manually writing frame_config.json on the bridge and restarting the JVM.
trigger: when a bridge commandResponse shows cmd=pairMeural success=false for an already-paired Meural
when RepairMeuralMqttProvisioning appears to succeed server-side but the bridge's frame_config.json never gains the new credentials

claim: As of 2026-04-15 staging.nimbusframe.net resolves to OVH stargate (51.81.243.11), whose nginx proxies HTTP to abydos and whose mosquitto serves MQTT, while ssh.nimbusframe.net still resolves to the Azure gateway (52.225.95.5) — so a bridge configured with the staging hostname is exercising OVH, not Azure.
trigger: before assuming a bridge pointed at staging.nimbusframe.net is hitting Azure
when verifying which environment a frame_config.json serverUrl or mqttBroker hostname reaches

claim: A Meural Canvas flashing/redrawing every ~45 seconds on a static JPG is expected behavior: MeuralDisplay.java:60-76 re-pushes the postcard every 45 seconds to stop Meural reverting to its built-in gallery after ~60 seconds, and the flash disappears once that art+frame combo is served as a looping per-frame MP4.
trigger: when a user reports a Meural flashing or redrawing every ~45 seconds on the same image
when bridge logs show only one Pushing line for an art item that visibly flashes repeatedly

claim: To force a MeuralBridge JVM to re-fetch all content from the server, wipe art/0, art/1, data, temp AND images/0, images/1 (Account-type media such as avatars) while preserving frame_config.json, unique, HWconfig.xml, config.xml, nimbus.json, meural.json, NimbusFrame.jks, serialNumber, logs/ and picFrame.current — wiping art/ alone leaves stale Account JPGs displaying for a full cycle.
trigger: before wiping a bridge's cache to test server-side crop fixes
when a wiped bridge still displays a stale wrong-orientation image sourced from images/ on the first rotation

claim: ArtVideoCache has no jobId column (schema: ArtVideoCacheId, MediaId, ProfileId, BlobPath, Status, GeneratedDate, LayoutVersion, FileSize, Duration, ErrorMessage, Target), so manually promoting stuck Status=processing rows from D:\Media\motion\v2 must match worker output files by the Art_{mediaId}_*.mp4 prefix, which suffices because each stuck row corresponds to one mediaId.

when trying to correlate a motion/v2 worker output file to an ArtVideoCache row

claim: Since the 2026-04-11 DNS cutover, staging.nimbusframe.net resolves to abydos on OVH (147.135.54.149), not Azure staging1, so 500s or odd behavior on 'staging' must be triaged in abydos IIS logs at D:\logs\picFrame_Web*.log rather than Azure.

claim: MSBuild publish only copies files with BuildAction=Content, so any new static file under picFrameWeb/Scripts/** must get a <Content Include> entry in picFrameWeb.csproj (git-tracking alone is not enough) or it 404s after deploy and the browser throws 'ReferenceError: X is not defined', as happened with nimbusUploader.js.
trigger: after git-adding any new .js/.css/.html file under picFrameWeb/Scripts
when the browser console shows a ReferenceError for a class whose script URL returns 404 after a deploy

claim: Both upload paths — web UI (DZUploader.ashx) and mobile API (POST /api/mobile/uploadMedia) — were verified working end-to-end on OVH abydos for image and video on 2026-04-15, so media upload is no longer a cutover blocker, superseding the hypothesis that saveAndProcessVideo's T-SQL breaks web video upload; this depends on the TagLibSharp csproj reference (commit 0ebb063d) staying deployed.
trigger: when assessing OVH cutover blockers for media upload paths
before modifying the TagLibSharp reference in picFrameWeb.csproj

claim: Before approving any cross-system port of code, schema objects, or triggers, require the dumped source body (e.g. SELECT OBJECT_DEFINITION(...)) rather than a reconstruction from column names — a guessed REPLACE(UUID(),'-','') port of trg_Frames_AutoGenerateCredentials would have created 32-char lowercase MQTT passwords where the fleet uses 36-char uppercase dashed UUIDs, a divergence auth would not catch.
trigger: before approving a DDL, trigger, or infra port justified from column names or reconstructed behavior
when an agent proposes porting an Azure SQL object to MySQL without pasting the Azure source

claim: nimbus-agent Supervisor.RestartAll() hangs during picFrame.jar OTA because Process.Stop() (process.go:257) spawns a second cmd.Wait() on an exec.Cmd that Process.run() is already waiting on — an illegal double Wait that stalls the sequential StopAll() loop, leaving some JVMs dead and others on old code; systemctl restart nimbus-agent recovers the bridge because reapOrphans() plus a fresh launch runs at agent start.
trigger: when an OTA update leaves some Meural JVMs stopped and others running old code with no keep-alive pings
when bridge logs show SIGINT sent to only a subset of JVMs and 'all processes stopped' never appears

claim: Loki on stargate labels all logs with service_name="web-server" (queries for job="nimbusservice" return nothing; extra filters are app="nimbus", environment="staging"), and only IIS/web app logs reach Loki — NimbusService logs stay in C:\logs on abydos.
trigger: before writing a Loki query for nimbus logs on stargate
when a Loki query for job="nimbusservice" returns no results

claim: As of 2026-04-16 stargate had no MySQL backup cron or systemd timer (only dpkg-db-backup.timer), and with NimbusJobs' DatabaseBackupJob flipped to Enabled=false the OVH MySQL databases were completely unprotected, so OVH cutover must not proceed until a mysqldump cron lands.
trigger: before an OVH cutover go/no-go assessment
when disabling DatabaseBackupJob in NimbusJobs

claim: An .aspx file present on disk but missing its Compile Include entries in picFrameWeb.csproj deploys the markup without compiling the code-behind into picFrameWeb.dll, producing HTTP 500 "Could not load type 'picFrameWeb.<page>'" — about.aspx hit this and needed 1 Content Include plus 2 Compile Include entries mirroring the default.aspx pattern.
trigger: when a deployed .aspx page returns HTTP 500 'Could not load type picFrameWeb.<page>'
after adding or restoring any .aspx file to picFrameWeb

claim: SchemaHealthCheck.CreateProcessTokensTable declared ActiveStop DATETIME(6) NOT NULL and omitted Azure's unique index on ProcessName, so any bootstrap-created table rejected every ProcessToken insert; corrected DDL (ActiveStop NULL plus UQ_ProcessTokens_ProcessName) was applied manually on stargate 2026-04-16, where lower_case_table_names=1 maps picFrame.ProcessTokens to picframe.processtokens.
trigger: when ProcessToken inserts fail on a bootstrap-created processtokens table
before trusting SchemaHealthCheck DDL to match the Azure schema exactly

claim: FrameXPlaylist is dead code from an unfinished multi-playlist feature (user-confirmed 2026-04-16): FrameSettings.currentPlayList is the playlist source of truth, the MQTT/v27 path reads FrameSettings only, stale FrameXPlaylist rows are expected, and no bugs should be filed or reconciliation attempted for it.
trigger: when FrameXPlaylist rows appear out of sync with MQTT retained config or FrameSettings
before filing a bug against or writing code that reads FrameXPlaylist

claim: Warhol's 2026-04-16 outage chain: picFrame.Frames.BridgeHwId drifted to NULL so DeviceConfigPublisher published a truncated retained bridge config listing only renoir, and nimbus-agent's reconcileMeurals (pre-030c918) treated it as authoritative and SIGINT'd warhol's JVM; the fix makes reconcileMeurals start-only, with removal requiring the explicit unpairMeural command, while the server-side BridgeHwId NULL drift remains unfixed and will recur.
trigger: when a Meural goes dark after a bridge reboot with the log line '<name> no longer in config — stopping'
when picFrame.Frames.BridgeHwId is NULL for a paired frame
before treating retained bridge/{uuid}/config as authoritative for tearing down running Meurals

claim: Dapper cannot coerce types across .NET positional-record constructors (exact match required), so MySQL return-type surprises — COUNT(*) is Int64 not Int32, IFNULL(date,'literal') promotes to String, TINYINT maps to sbyte/byte — throw 'A parameterless default constructor or one matching signature (type list) is required'; fix by matching record parameter types to the SQL shape in the error message, not by converting records to settable-property classes.
trigger: when Dapper throws InvalidOperationException 'parameterless default constructor or one matching signature (type list) is required' for a record DTO
before writing a positional record DTO for a MySQL aggregate or IFNULL query

claim: A frames-team session recorded learning_e3f (nimbus-agent 1.15.0 source drift / park hygiene) and learning_097 (the reconcileMeurals bug chain with Layer 1/Layer 2 fix rationale).
trigger: when searching project nimbus for frames-team learnings about nimbus-agent 1.15.0 source drift or reconcileMeurals

claim: deploy.sh excludes NimbusService.exe.config from ovh-* bundles (lines 344-353), so config values like Max Pool Size are changed by editing the file directly on abydos over SSH (backup first, use single-quoted PowerShell -replace on a unique stable string), and the next deploy preserves the edit and restarts the service; providerName remains System.Data.SqlClient by design because a custom factory resolves the real MySQL driver at runtime.
trigger: before changing NimbusService.exe.config values such as connection strings or Max Pool Size on abydos
when a NimbusService config edit needs to survive deploy.sh ovh-staging

claim: The Azure gateway (10.7.0.1) runs an nginx stream proxy for inbound TCP 36004 to staging2 (10.0.3.5:36004) configured at /etc/nginx/streams/combined.conf and logging to /var/log/nginx/stream-access.log, so frame-to-server TCP attempts can be observed at the gateway (grep by source IP, check TCP 502s) even when NimbusService shows no activity for a frame.
trigger: when NimbusService shows no activity for a frame and you need to confirm whether its TCP SYNs reach the server
when scoping fleet-wide frame connections or proxy 502s on TCP port 36004

claim: Xfinity xFi Advanced Security can heuristically quarantine a frame generating rapid identical outbound connections (e.g. a 20-second reconnect loop), and the block is cloud-backed so gateway reboots do not clear it — the customer must unblock the device in the Xfinity app or disable Advanced Security, and a cellular-only phone hotspot test isolates whether xFi is the blocker.
trigger: when a previously-working frame goes completely silent on an Xfinity network while other devices work
when a frame stays offline even after the customer reboots their Xfinity gateway

claim: staging2 (Azure production, private IP 10.0.3.5) accepts direct SSH from the local Windows machine with no ProxyCommand (ssh -i /c/code/Nimbus/keys/id_ed25519 tlemmons@10.0.3.5, PowerShell shell), unlike the Azure gateway 10.7.0.1 which requires a stargate jump; authoritative frame-connection events are in C:\logs\NimbusService<date>.log alongside picFrameError.log and picFrame_Web*.log.
trigger: before setting up a ProxyCommand jump to reach staging2 at 10.0.3.5
when looking for authoritative frame-connection events on Azure production

trigger: when investigating Frame 518 (UUID 61ea5cec-3fe5-4df0-9531-0b00380aa7c8) reconnect-loop or offline reports
before attributing a frame's 20-second reconnect loop to PaymentDue validation or a server deploy

claim: Frames can show falsely online indefinitely because removeOnlineframe/PublishOffline only run from PicFrame.Shutdown() on a socket event, ownership checks skip removal during reconnect flaps (isStillOwner=false), and no background reaper scans stale CommTime — Frame 518's silently-dead socket left Redis OnlineStatus and retained MQTT frame/{uuid}/status/online=true stale until manually flipped with a retained mosquitto_pub of 'false'.

before writing a mitigation for stale frame online status (retained status/online=false triggers MqttOnlineStatusHandler's offline branch)

claim: On stargate MySQL 8.0.45, root@localhost uses caching_sha2_password with an EMPTY password and debian-sys-maint does not exist, so admin scripts must use 'sudo mysql --no-defaults -u root'; additionally /root is mode 0700 so file tests need 'sudo test -f' and glob expansion under /root or /var/backups/mysql must run inside 'sudo bash -c'.

before writing admin or backup scripts that access MySQL or paths under /root on stargate
